{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Detlef Lienau (February 17, 1818 Uetersen – August 29, 1887) was a German architect born in Holstein.","title":"Detlef Lienau"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" He is credited with having introduced the French style to American building construction, notably the mansard roof and all its decorative flourishes.","title":"Detlef Lienau"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" Trained at L’Ecole des Beaux-Arts in Paris, he designed virtually every type of Victorian structure—cottages, mansions, townhouses, apartment houses, hotels, tenements, banks, stores, churches, schools, libraries, offices, factories, railroad stations, and a museum.","title":"Detlef Lienau"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" Lienau was recognized by clients and colleagues alike as one of the most creative and technically proficient architects of the period, and was one of the 29 founding members of the American Institute of Architects.","title":"Detlef Lienau"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Maurice Milliere (1871–1946) was a French painter, printmaker and illustrator, born in Le Havre to upper working class parents; his father was a merchant's clerk.","title":"Maurice Milliere"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" His early artistic interests are not known, but he completed his secondary education at the Ecole De Beaux Arts in Le Havre before travelling to Paris in 1889 to continue his studies at the l'Ecole des Arts Decoratifs and l'Ecole des Beaux-Arts.","title":"Maurice Milliere"}],"peer_messages":["Unverified peer answer: noanswer"],"previous_answer":"noanswer","question":"Where is the historic meeting venue built in a style taught at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts?"}
